subject.title: feat(feeds): refresh and manage followed publishers

question: Should OpenClaw core own signed publisher-feed following, persistent state, background refresh, and five Gateway RPCs, or should the feed-specific workflow move behind a plugin or ClawHub-owned surface?
rationale: The patch is not a mechanical bug fix: it establishes a new long-lived core control plane and trust boundary, so maintainers must choose its product and ownership model before a repair or merge path is safe.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core seam
options.body: Approve only the minimum generic Gateway and plugin seam needed, then move publisher-specific transport, trust, refresh policy, and state ownership to the selected owner.

options.title: Adopt the full core control plane
options.body: Explicitly accept the CLI, RPC, scheduler, remote fetch, and shared-state contracts as supported OpenClaw core behavior.

options.title: Route the workflow outside core
options.body: Close or replace this branch with a ClawHub/plugin implementation if existing extension seams can host the signed publisher-feed feature.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core seam
recommendation.body: Approve only the minimum generic Gateway and plugin seam needed, then move publisher-specific transport, trust, refresh policy, and state ownership to the selected owner.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the only identifiable person connected across the linked proposal stack; a core owner must provide the actual sponsorship decision.
